definition: Strong consistency means a read returns the most recent write that succeeded, so clients do not observe stale or divergent values. The strict form is linearizability: operations appear to happen in one order that respects real time. Providing it across a partition often means refusing some requests rather than answering with a stale value.
examples: A read-after-write that always sees the write
A leader that serves reads only when it is sure it is still leader
